subject: Commit-bridge and pool transition: short-term GPU capacity plan
messages:
From: Colin Park <colin.park@orionai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term commit bridge and smoothing options

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this on. We ran into a couple of surprise spikes in Q3 — attached is a compact export (CSV) showing peak windows where our p95 token consumption jumped ~3.6x for ~2–6 hour windows. We expect at least two similar spikes in Q4 driven by a rollout and a marketing campaign.

Our immediate ask: we need a path to avoid dropped requests while we finalize our Dedicated commit (we're close, but procurement needs two weeks to route a PO). Can Redwood provide:
- a short-term burst or temporary pool we can draw from for up to 30 days, or
- a commit-bridge (one-off tranche) that buys us guaranteed GPUs for the next 60 days with a credit against the final committed amount?

Budget: we can allocate up to $65k for the interim solution if it avoids outages.

Appreciate a quick outline of viable options and cost. Happy to take a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Colin Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Orion AI

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term commit bridge and smoothing options

Colin — thanks for the data dump, that helped. I sketched two pragmatic options that will avoid request drops during your procurement window and make the final commit cleaner. See the attached proposal and spreadsheet for line-item economics. High level:

Option A — Burst pool (30 days)
- We provision a GPU burst pool (Nvidia A100-equivalent) dedicated for your tenant for transient surges.
- Billing: flat daily capacity fee + per-token overage when the pool is used. Estimated cost: ~$52k for 30 days given the spike profile you sent.
- Fast: can stand up within 48 hours after signed SOW.

Option B — Commit-bridge tranche (60 days)
- You purchase a time-limited tranche (committed GPU-hours) that acts as guaranteed capacity.
- We apply 100% of that spend as a credit against your final 12-month Dedicated commitment if you convert.
- Estimated cost: ~$60k for 60 days; this converts to a credit that reduces the effective first-year commit.

Tradeoffs: burst pool is fastest and lower upfront; commit-bridge gives you cost certainty and credits against the eventual contract. Either path avoids live throttling during peaks.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick call Monday morning (30 min) to pick A vs B and confirm SOW points.
2) Ben to prepare a billing addendum and PO-ready quote.
3) Karthik to confirm capacity schedule and any lead times for GPU allocation.

I attached: redwood-commit-bridge-proposal-v1.pdf and commit-breakdown-q4.xlsx.

If that looks reasonable I'll put a draft SOW on the HubSpot deal and we can route it.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-commit-bridge-proposal-v1.pdf; commit-breakdown-q4.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Internal: Orion AI interim capacity — need numbers and terms (quick)

Logan — quick notes from infra:
- Burst pool: we can stand up a 10-GPU burst pool reserved for Orion in ~36 hours if we reassign from flexible capacity. Warmup: first 4–6 hours of elevated latency expected while model KV caches populate; recommend an initial smooth-shift tactic (send warmup traffic at 50% peak for 2 hours).
- Commit-bridge tranche: operationally identical once allocated; difference is the billing record and guaranteed hours. We can allocate up to 16 GPUs for 60 days but that reduces available flexible inventory for other bursts — estimate risk window is manageable given current pipeline.
- Constraints: to preserve latency SLOs we need a short pre-warm window and KV-cache priming. Also, if Orion routes traffic from a new region we need an extra 12–24 hour lead time.

I'll update the capacity calendar and tag a tentative allocation. If Ben confirms billing terms we can finalize the quote to Orion today.

— Karthik
